thread:
natalie: :warning: Incident notice 11 0Dedicated capacity starvation in apac-sg1. Reserved pools reporting allocation failures and burst autoscale not firing. Some Dedicated customers seeing 429s and long queue times. Status: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/2211234567

ops-bot: Incident INC-2211234567 opened. Tags: dedicated, apac-sg1, reserved-capacity, customer-impact. Runbook: https://git.redwood.ai/incidents/runbooks/dedicated-allocation-failure

quentin: Impact: ~12% of Dedicated reservations impacted, surge of allocation failures around 03:12 SGT. Affected tenants primarily on gpu-type a100-40g. Errors: `allocation_error: no_suitable_node` and controller logs show repeated placement retries.

harpreet: Hypothesis: a node-labeling job mis-applied a taint on a subset of hosts during last-night maintenance, making them ineligible for reserved pools, effectively shrinking available capacity. Reproducer: labels: `maintenance=hold` present on 18 nodes.

sophia: Mitigations started: 1) emergency lift of taint on eligible nodes, 2) manual placement reserved eviction for highest-severity customers, 3) temporary enable of burst-autoscale fallback to on-demand in apac-sg1. Executed at 03:26 SGT.

natalie: Can the sched team avoid restarting the allocation controller until we've verified reclaimed nodes are stable? Restarts trigger re-evaluation storms. @quentin @harpreet

quentin: Ack. No controller restarts. I've untainted 15 nodes at 03:29 SGT; allocation failures dropped immediately. p95 allocation latency back to baseline after 03:35 SGT for most reservations. Metrics: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/scheduler/apac-sg1-reserved-capacity

ops-bot: Update INC-2211234567: mitigations applied. Temporary on-demand fallback remains enabled while we validate stability. Customer comms: draft ready, will send targeted update to affected accounts.

sales-ops: Please include recommended short-term workaround: switch traffic to Hosted or Dedicated with smaller GPU SKUs if possible. We'll coordinate outreach.

harpreet: Root cause fix: remove faulty label sync job from maintenance pipeline and add an e2e check to detect tainted-node count regressions. Patch PR #8732. Planning rollout tomorrow 02:00 SGT after a small dry-run.

sophia: Final update 03:50 SGT: full capacity restored, on-demand fallback disabled. Observability shows no further allocation failures. Postmortem owners: harpreet + quentin. Postmortem doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/incidents/2211234567/postmortem

natalie: :white_check_mark: Thanks all. If you see residual allocation errors, add traces/logs here and tag me. We'll follow up in the postmortem with customer impact table.
